import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a consistent order for 'size' for better visualization
size_order = ['Small', 'Medium', 'Large']
df['size'] = pd.Categorical(df['size'], categories=size_order, ordered=True)

# Aggregate total sales by product and size
# This will calculate the sum of 'total' for each unique combination of 'product' and 'size'
aggregated_sales = df.groupby(['product', 'size'])['total'].sum().reset_index()

# Set a visually appealing style for the plot
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a grouped bar chart to visualize total sales by product and size
sns.barplot(
    data=aggregated_sales,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='size',
    palette='viridis'  # Choose a color palette for different sizes
)

# Add a descriptive title to the plot
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Size', fontsize=16)

# Label the x-axis
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)

# Label the y-axis
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)

# Rotate x-axis labels for better readability, especially if product names are long
plt.xticks(rotation=45, ha='right')

# Add a legend to distinguish between different sizes
plt.legend(title='Size', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# Adjust layout to prevent labels from overlapping and ensure everything fits
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Define a consistent order for 'size' for better visualization

# Aggregate total sales by product and size
# This will calculate the sum of 'total' for each unique combination of 'product' and 'size'

# Set a visually appealing style for the plot
sns.set_style("whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes for the plot
plt.figure(figsize=(12, 7))

# Create a grouped bar chart to visualize total sales by product and size
sns.barplot(
    data=aggregated_sales,
    x='product',
    y='total',
    hue='size',
    palette='viridis'  # Choose a color palette for different sizes
)

# Add a descriptive title to the plot
plt.title('Total Sales by Product and Size', fontsize=16)

# Label the x-axis
plt.xlabel('Product', fontsize=12)

# Label the y-axis
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=12)
